intro: Complete You Do first. Show working for each question. Reveal the model answer, method and marking points before self-marking.

questions.title: Outputs from an adder
questions.prompt: A digital circuit adds binary digits. Name its two output signals and explain why a full adder needs a third input.
questions.answer: Sum (S) and Carry-out (Cout). A full adder also accepts Carry-in (Cin) from a previous column.
steps: Identify the result bit produced in this column: Sum.
Identify the bit passed to the next column: Carry-out.
Explain that adding multi-bit values may require a carry from the preceding column.
marksBreak: 1 mark: a full adder accepts a carry-in/third input.

questions.title: Half-adder truth table
questions.prompt: For the four pairs A,B = 00, 01, 10 and 11, write the outputs Sum and Carry-out for a half adder. Show each row as AB → Sum,Carry.
steps: Sum is A XOR B: it is 1 when exactly one input is 1.
Carry-out is A AND B: it is 1 only when both inputs are 1.
For 1+1, binary 10 means Sum=0 and Carry-out=1.

questions.title: Draw a half adder
questions.prompt: Draw a logic circuit with inputs P and R and outputs S and C. It must add two one-bit values. Label both gates and draw the input connections to each.
questions.answer: P and R feed an XOR gate producing S; P and R also feed an AND gate producing C.
steps: Branch each input so that P and R reach both gates.
Connect P and R to XOR; label its output S.
Connect P and R to AND; label its output C.
marksBreak: 1 mark: correct connections from both inputs to both gates and outputs correctly labelled.

questions.title: Work out a full-adder result
questions.prompt: A full adder receives A=1, B=0 and Cin=1. Calculate the decimal total of the three inputs. Determine Sum and Cout. Then state the outputs if A=1, B=1 and Cin=1.
questions.answer: For 1+0+1=2 (binary 10): Sum=0, Cout=1. For 1+1+1=3 (binary 11): Sum=1, Cout=1.
steps: Add the three inputs as individual binary digits.
The right-hand (least significant) bit is Sum.
Check both cases by writing 2 as 10₂ and 3 as 11₂.
marksBreak: 1 mark: first case Sum=0 and Cout=1.
1 mark: second case Sum=1 and Cout=1.

questions.title: Design a full-adder circuit
questions.prompt: Design a full adder using only two XOR gates, two AND gates and one OR gate. Inputs are A, B and Cin. Draw and label the intermediate signal X and the final Sum and Cout outputs.
questions.answer: X=A XOR B; Sum=X XOR Cin; Cout=(A AND B) OR (X AND Cin).
steps: Use the first XOR to calculate X=A XOR B.
Use the second XOR to calculate Sum=X XOR Cin.
Use an AND gate on A and B.
Use another AND gate on X and Cin.
Use OR to combine the two AND outputs into Cout. The first AND output must not feed the second AND gate.
marksBreak: 1 mark: first XOR takes A and B.
1 mark: second XOR takes X and Cin and produces Sum.
1 mark: first AND takes A and B.
1 mark: second AND takes X and Cin.
1 mark: OR joins both AND outputs to produce Cout with correct wiring.
